newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Court rules in favour of News appeal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Court rules in favour of News appeal.

text.p: Media tycoon Rupert Murdoch on Friday won legal approval to launch his rebel Super League competition in Australia.
The Federal Court of Australia upheld Murdoch's appeal against an earlier court ruling which banned his rugby league competition from kicking off in Australia before the year 2000.

Murdoch, whose News Ltd media organisation has provided the financial backing for Super League, has been embroiled in a bitter power struggle with the sport's national body, the Australian Rugby League (ARL), for almost two years.
Super League was originally scheduled to kick-off in March this year but Murdoch was forced to shelve the plans after losing a court battle with the ARL in February.
The court ruled that the clubs must honour loyalty agreements binding them to play in the existing ARL premiership competition until the end of the 1999 season.
Murdoch has invested A$270 million in the rebel rugby league competition, winning the loyalty of eight existing Australian clubs and more than 200 players.
He has also signed up clubs in Britain and New Zealand for a similar rebel competition.
The court said it found the loyalty agreements linking clubs with the ARL contravened sections of Australia's anti-monopoly, trade practices act.

"Since the commitments and loyalty agreements are void, the full court has decided that the trial judge's orders, in so far as they were based on the assumption that the agreements are enforceable, can not stand," the court said in its judgement.
"The result of the present appeal...is that the appeals have been allowed and all orders made by the trial judge have been set aside," the court said.
